en.text: Article 12(2) and (3)(b) — The source-State limitation in paragraph 2 applies only to royalties mentioned in sub-paragraph (a) of paragraph 3: ‘However, the royalties mentioned in sub-paragraph a) of paragraph 3 may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise ... but ... the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.’ Paragraph 3(b) separately identifies ‘any copyright of literary, artistic or scientific work including cinematograph films and films or tapes for television or radio broadcasting.’

Article 12(2) and (3)(a) — ‘However, the royalties mentioned in sub-paragraph a) of paragraph 3 may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.’ Paragraph 3(a) covers patents, trade marks, designs or models, plans, secret formulae or processes, computer software, industrial, commercial or scientific equipment, and information concerning industrial, commercial or scientific experience.
